evidence_quotes.quote: This paper seeks to identify the key drivers of water and sanitation PPP financing in Zimbabwe; and
In sync with [52,58], the dependent variable (PPPUSD) was the investment value of PPPs that reached financial closure.

To manage the adverse consequences of multicollinearity and the loss of explanatory power, the six governance variables (control of corruption, CC; regulatory quality, RQ; rule of law, RL; voice and accountability, VA; political stability, PS; and government effectiveness, GE) were examined separately, and hence, seven models were estimated.

The sample frame was from 1996 to 2021. The choice of time frame was rationalised on the basis that, in Zimbabwe, being an infant PPP market, it was in the late 1990s that the pioneering PPP contract was signed. The sample frame provided 25 data points that the researchers considered reasonable, given that this is a single-country analysis.

criterion_notes.c1: Does not examine household or community water or sanitation service access; instead, it investigates macroeconomic, financial-market, and macro-governance determinants of Public-Private Partnership (PPP) infrastructure project financing in Zimbabwe and proposes a PPP financing framework. Service unreliability is mentioned only as introductory background.
criterion_notes.c2: Under the plain wording of Criterion 2, the study passes because it tests six country-level Worldwide Governance Indicators (control of corruption, regulatory quality, rule of law, voice and accountability, political stability, and government effectiveness) as explanatory variables in Tobit regressions. Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type clarification, Criterion 2 is NOT met because these aggregate WGI percentile ranks are macro-governance indicators analysed only as determinants of PPP capital investment flows rather than a rule-type mechanism (such as eligibility screening, documentation/tenure rules, tariff/cost-recovery rules, administrative burden, discretion, enforcement, or utility regulatory structure) directly governing household or community service access. Note that even under the plain Criterion 2 reading, the overall study decision remains exclude because Criteria 1 and 4 fail.
criterion_notes.c3: Contains quantitative empirical analysis applying Tobit econometric regression models to 25 years of secondary time-series data (1996-2021) from the World Bank PPI, WDI, and WGI databases, Central Statistics Office Zimbabwe, and Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports no outcome measuring water or sanitation access, connection, availability, reliability, continuity, quantity, affordability, or exclusion. The sole empirical dependent variable (PPPUSD) is the USD investment value of water and sanitation PPP infrastructure projects reaching financial closure.
criterion_notes.c5: Unit of analysis (country-level annual time series for Zimbabwe, 1996-2021, 25 annual observations), exposures (macroeconomic, financial development, and WGI governance indicators), outcome (first-differenced log USD investment value of PPPs reaching financial closure), and study design (time-series Tobit econometric analysis) are clearly identifiable, though not at a service-access level.

study_design: Quantitative longitudinal country-level time-series econometric study using Tobit regression (1996-2021)
population_and_sample: Country-level annual macro-financial time series for Zimbabwe covering 1996 to 2021 (25 annual observations of water and sanitation PPP financial closures)
exposure: Macroeconomic indicators (GDP per capita, reserves-to-imports ratio, inflation, net FDI), financial market indicators (stock market capitalisation, domestic bank credit, bank credit-to-deposits, non-performing loans), and six Worldwide Governance Indicators percentile ranks (control of corruption, regulatory quality, rule of law, voice and accountability, political stability, government effectiveness)
outcome: USD investment value of water and sanitation Public-Private Partnership (PPP) infrastructure projects reaching financial closure (first-differenced natural logarithm, delta logPPPUSD)
rationale: Note on metadata: the retrieved PDF is the 2024 MDPI Water journal publication (Mundonde & Makoni, 2024) of Justice Mundonde's 2022 work of the exact same title. Excluded (E04 - Wrong outcome; also fails C1 and narrow C2). Although the paper empirically models water and sanitation sector data in Zimbabwe using Tobit regressions (1996-2021), its dependent variable is solely the USD investment value of PPP infrastructure projects reaching financial closure (PPPUSD), with no empirical measure of household or community water or sanitation service access, connection, availability, reliability, quantity, affordability, or exclusion. Furthermore, under the 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 clarification, the six aggregate Worldwide Governance Indicators tested are macro-governance Determinants of project finance rather than rule-type mechanisms directly governing user access to services. Even under the plain wording of Criterion 2, the paper remains excluded because it examines macro project finance rather than service access and reports no eligible access outcome.
